title: Affine-target diagonal pairs and their normalized DNC comparison
statement:
Work at the finite coefficient stage of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and $A=\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be separated, of finite type, and smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the exceptional inverse image and finite derived pullbacks [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and put $\omega_h=Rh^!A$ for every indicated separated finite-type morphism $h$.

There is a finite affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_iV_i$ with $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ and each $B_i$ finitely generated over $k$. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ with $B$ finitely generated over $k$, put $X_V=X\times_YV$, $j_V:X_V\hookrightarrow X$, $f_V:X_V\to V$, $W_V=X_V\times_VX_V$, with projections $p_{1,V},p_{2,V}$ and diagonal $\Delta_V:X_V\to W_V$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $X_V$ and $W_V$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $f_V,p_{1,V},p_{2,V}$ are separated finite-type morphisms smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. There is the canonical restriction isomorphism
$$\rho_V:Lj_V^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f_V},$$
namely the base-change isomorphism of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3) for the Cartesian square of $f$ along the open immersion $V\hookrightarrow Y$.
The diagonal is a regular closed immersion of pure codimension $d$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]: locally its ideal is generated by a regular sequence of length $d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], allowing the empty sequence when $d=0$. Moreover $p_{1,V}\Delta_V=\operatorname{id}_{X_V}$, and its normal bundle $N_V=N_{\Delta_V/W_V}\cong T_{X_V/V}$ [pur9-dg-def-tangent], by the canonical isomorphism of [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion] for $f_V$, is a vector bundle of rank $d$ with projection $\pi_V:N_V\to X_V$ and zero section $z_V$ [def-pur-normal-bundle]. For the section invariant $C(g,s)=Ls^*Rg^!A$ [def-pur-section-invariant], there are the diagonal base-change isomorphism $\alpha_V$ of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] for $f_V$ and the normalized DNC isomorphism $\delta_V$ of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] for the pair $(g,s)=(p_{1,V},\Delta_V)$ over $B=X_V$
$$\alpha_V:C(p_{1,V},\Delta_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f_V},\qquad
\delta_V:C(p_{1,V},\Delta_V)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_V,z_V).$$
Thus $\delta_V$ is the unique isomorphism that is the identity on the standard section invariant in etale coordinates [def-weil-etale-morphism] taking the pair near its section to $(\mathbf A^d_{X_V}\to X_V,0)$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Absolute separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ is not required.

source.place: Step 1, the diagonal section invariant and its tangent normal bundle; affine-target domain verification and normalized DNC comparison (returned proof Steps 1--2)

proof.text: Apply the finite-affine-cover characterization in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] to the structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: the target is affine, so its inverse image $Y$ has a finite affine open cover $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with each $B_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. In fact [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], applied to that structure morphism and any affine open $V\subseteq Y$, shows that its coordinate algebra is finitely generated over $k$. This proves the cover assertion without assuming $Y$ separated. If $Y$ is empty the finite cover can be empty.

source.place: Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type; Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize (2),(4); affine-target preparation for blueprint Step 1

proof.text: Fix any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ as in the statement. The open subscheme $f^{-1}(V)\subseteq X$ has the universal property of $X\times_YV$: a map into $X$ whose composite into $Y$ factors through $V$ factors uniquely through this open subscheme, with the restricted structure sheaf. Thus identify $X_V$ with this open subscheme and $j_V$ with its open immersion, using [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. The square with sides $j_V$, $f_V$, $f$ and $V\hookrightarrow Y$ is Cartesian. Define $W_V=X_V\times_VX_V$ by the same fibre-product convention.

source.place: Step 1, affine-target localization before forming the diagonal pair

proof.text: The morphism $f_V$ is the base change of the given separated finite-type $f$, so [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] makes $f_V$ separated and of finite type. Both $p_{1,V}$ and $p_{2,V}$ are base changes of $f_V$ (the two copies of $X_V$ have the same map to $V$); apply the same result to obtain separatedness and finite type for both. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1) first to $f$ along $V\to Y$, then to $f_V$ along itself. This gives smoothness of pure relative dimension $d$ for $f_V$ and both projections. The base-change maps need no smoothness, flatness, or absolute separatedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01T4, lemma-base-change-finite-type; Tag 01VB, lemma-base-change-smooth; Tag 02NK, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d; schemes.tex Tag 01KU, lemma-separated-permanence (3); blueprint Step 1

proof.text: Since $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and the target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has only its whole nonempty affine open, its structure morphism is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism], hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). It is of finite type because $B$ is finitely generated over $k$. The structure morphism of $X_V$ is $X_V\xrightarrow{f_V}V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; that of $W_V$ is $W_V\xrightarrow{p_{1,V}}X_V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply separated composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) and finite-type composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) to these two composites. Therefore $X_V,W_V$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. This is precisely the absolute domain needed for DNC; neither the map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ nor the map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ has been asserted separated.

source.place: Tags 01S6/01S7, definition-affine and lemma-affine-separated; Tag 01T3, lemma-composition-finite-type; schemes.tex Tag 01KU, lemma-separated-permanence (1); domain check for blueprint Step 1

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](3) to the Cartesian square of Step 2. Its vertical map is the given smooth separated finite-type $f$ and its base change is $f_V$, with the same finite coefficient ring $A$. Its upper horizontal map is $j_V$. The stated canonical base-change isomorphism is consequently $Lj_V^*Rf^!A\simeq Rf_V^!A$, which is exactly $\rho_V:Lj_V^*\omega_f\simeq\omega_{f_V}$. The theorem permits arbitrary base change, so the open immersion of the lower horizontal map is allowed.

source.place: Step 1 and final base-change paragraph: restriction of the orientation-free dualizing object, using cohomological smoothness (3)

proof.text: Use exists_isRegular_smooth_diagonal_generators [lem-sc-smooth-diagonal-regular-immersion] at each point of the diagonal. Its alternative unit-ideal case is impossible there: restriction sends 1 to 0, whereas the germ at that source point gives a nontrivial section ring. This supplies a regular sequence of length d, including the empty sequence when d=0. Relative differentials are finite locally free of rank d by [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free]. For the canonical normal/tangent comparison, use the proved algebraic helpers of [lem-pur-chart-normal-differential]: differenceIdentification sends da to the class of p2*a-p1*a; diagonalSymmetric identifies the symmetric algebra with the associated graded; normalTangentIdentification passes to relative Spec, preserving projection and zero. Compose with the normalized Rees comparison of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-interfaces]. Its normalization and naturality give the displayed equation on every differential generator. For uniqueness, first use uniqueness of the normalized Rees comparison. Equality on da gives equality on all differentials by their universal property, then equality on the symmetric algebra by its universal property, and finally equality of scheme maps by relative-Spec faithfulness. The needed Noetherian hypothesis follows from finite type over the field; it adds no hypothesis to the statement.

source.place: Step 1: the diagonal is a closed section and its normal bundle is the rank-d relative tangent bundle; lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion statement and proof

proof.text: For $f_V$, [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] gives the canonical isomorphism $\omega_{p_{1,V}}\simeq Lp_{2,V}^*\omega_{f_V}$ and explicitly its diagonal-pullback consequence $C(p_{1,V},\Delta_V)\simeq\omega_{f_V}$. Take precisely the latter isomorphism, constructed there by pulling back the base-change map along $\Delta_V$ and using $p_{2,V}\Delta_V=\operatorname{id}_{X_V}$, as $\alpha_V$. Its statement already supplies this composite and its canonicity, so no separate pullback-composition claim is needed here.

source.place: Step 2, first sentence: the left side is omega_f by diagonal base change

proof.text: Apply [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to the smooth separated finite-type first projection and its closed diagonal section over X_V. Steps 3--6 supply its geometric hypotheses, with d=0 allowed. Its existence-and-uniqueness theorem has precisely the published family equation used by AffineDiagonalDncNormalized, so no comparison is replaced by an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism. To identify the recorded sectionInvariantFinite source with this same source under the intrinsic derived equivalence, compare the tensor unit with the intrinsic constant coefficient object using [def-pur-proetale-constant-module-unit], its degree-zero derived realization, and the module equivalence of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The derived functor composition isomorphisms intertwine upper star with intrinsic pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Transporting the coefficient-unit isomorphism through the fixed exceptional functor then identifies the dualizing objects and hence their section pullbacks [def-pur-section-invariant]. All these comparison maps are constructed, not assumed.

source.place: Step 1: apply DNC invariance to (p_1, Delta); final paragraph: canonicity from its uniqueness clause
